newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight falls to 5.9/6.0 pct on bill maturity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight falls to 5.9/6.0 pct on bill maturity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 5.9/6.0 percent as market liquidity improved further due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday, dealers said.
A one-billion ringgit bill issue had matured on Wednesday.
Both the maturities were not rolled over.
The overnight traded from a high of 6.7 percent, against 6.5-7.0 percent on Thursday.
"The overnight was expected to fall because of the maturity. Banks are also getting long on the overnight," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Earlier, one-week money was at 7.50 percent against 7.80 percent on Thursday.
One- and three-month money were at 7.70/80 percent against 7.8/8.0 percent.
Dealers said maturity of another Bank Negara bill issue worth 500 million ringgit next week could push rates lower.

But an outflow of some two billion ringgit on June 26 due to maturity of funds Bank Negara lent to the market to help ease a liquidity squeeze last month could prevent rates from falling back to a month ago levels, they said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were marginally lower.
At 0830 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down one point to 92.52, or an implied yield of 7.48 percent.
The December contract fell two to 92.62, or 7.38 percent and March 1998 was also down two to 92.70, or 7.30 percent.
